title: Quantum Yang-Mills existence with a mass gap

concept.text: A mathematically rigorous construction of quantum Yang-Mills theory on four-dimensional space-time for any compact simple gauge group, proving a positive mass gap. Sources given: https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/ ; https://world-of-mathematics.com/blog/millennium-problems-overview/.

page.title: Quantum Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
page.definition: For every compact simple gauge group, which specifies the internal symmetry, the goal is to construct an interacting quantum theory of Yang–Mills fields without matter on all of four-dimensional space-time. In each such theory there must be an energy Δ > 0 such that every excitation lies at least Δ above the vacuum, the state of lowest energy.

goal.need: Classical gluon waves are massless, and the energy gap is zero at every order of perturbation theory. A proof would establish that gluon interactions alone produce a positive excitation threshold. Physicists already use lattice estimates of glueball masses to interpret particle data: one search examined 10.1 billion J/ψ events. The proof would give the threshold a continuum foundation. Its numerical value would still require calculation, and identifying a measured resonance also requires accounting for mixing with states containing quarks.

statements.quote: Quantum Yang-Mills theory is now the foundation of most of elementary particle theory

statements.body: Clay Mathematics Institute, founding Scientific Advisory Board
statements.quote: The seven Millennium Prize Problems were chosen by the founding Scientific Advisory Board of CMI
statements.context: Yang–Mills existence and mass gap was one of the seven problems announced in Paris on 24 May 2000.

completion.title: Yang–Mills theory exists on R⁴ with a positive mass gap for every compact simple gauge group.
completion.criterion: For every compact simple gauge group G, construct nontrivial pure quantum Yang–Mills theory on R⁴ with axioms at least as strong as the Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader formulations, the prescribed local gauge-invariant observables and short-distance asymptotics. Prove that the Hamiltonian H, with vacuum energy zero, has no spectrum in (0,Δ) for some Δ > 0, and that m = inf(spec(H)∖{0}) is finite.
completion.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Jaffe–Witten official problem description, §4.
completion.threshold_quote: Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory exists on R⁴ and has a mass gap Δ > 0.
completion.basis: Clay lists the combined problem as unsolved. The Yang–Mills group’s November 2026 assessment reports an infinite-volume construction along subsequences, with a Wightman theory in each pure phase. The assessment leaves the mass gap and uniqueness across subsequences open. Clay requires publication in a qualifying outlet, at least two years since publication, and general mathematical acceptance before it considers a prize.

milestones.title: The Wilson SU(N) lattice transfer matrix is self-adjoint and strictly positive on physical states.
milestones.criterion: For four-dimensional Wilson SU(N) lattice gauge theory at spacing a > 0 and finite spatial volume, construct the operator T that advances Euclidean time by one lattice step. On the Hilbert space of gauge-invariant states, prove T = T* and ⟨ψ,Tψ⟩ > 0 for every nonzero ψ, so that H = −a⁻¹ log T defines a self-adjoint Hamiltonian.
milestones.set_by: Constructive quantum field theory’s physical-positivity criterion; Lüscher (1977), for SU(N).
milestones.threshold_quote: Construction of a selfadjoint, strictly positive transfer matrix for Euclidean lattice gauge theories

milestones.title: Pure SU(2) correlation functions have an ultraviolet limit at fixed infrared cutoff.
milestones.criterion: Construct the Euclidean correlation functions of four-dimensional pure SU(2) Yang–Mills theory in the trivial topological sector and a regularized axial gauge. Remove the short-distance cutoff with the long-distance cutoff fixed, and establish the Slavnov identities expressing infinitesimal gauge invariance.
milestones.set_by: Constructive quantum field theory’s cutoff-removal test; Magnen, Rivasseau and Sénéor (1993), for SU(2) under the stated restrictions.
milestones.threshold_quote: with a fixed infrared cutoff but no ultraviolet cutoff, in a regularized axial gauge.

milestones.title: Continuum quantum Yang–Mills theory is constructed on a four-dimensional torus.
milestones.criterion: Construct pure quantum Yang–Mills theory on a four-torus T⁴ of fixed physical size. Define its renormalized local gauge-invariant fields and their Euclidean correlation functions with the short-distance cutoff removed, and establish the field-theory properties appropriate to the torus, including reflection positivity.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Jaffe–Witten official problem description, §6.5.

milestones.title: Continuum finite-volume Yang–Mills theories have a positive mass gap uniform in volume.
milestones.criterion: For continuum finite-volume Yang–Mills approximations, prove one lower bound Δ > 0 on excitation energies above the vacuum that remains valid as the volume tends to infinity.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Jaffe–Witten official problem description, §§5–6.5.

milestones.title: A finite four-dimensional lattice defines pure Yang–Mills observables with exact gauge invariance.
milestones.criterion: At fixed positive lattice spacing and finite volume, assign a gauge-group element to each oriented link, with inversion on reversal. Define expectations by integrating with product Haar measure and the Wilson plaquette weight, normalized by the partition function. Show that local gauge transformations preserve the measure and action.
milestones.set_by: Wilson’s lattice formulation of gauge theory, as used in constructive quantum field theory.
milestones.threshold_quote: on a discrete lattice in Euclidean space-time, preserving exact gauge invariance

milestones.title: An infinite-volume limit of Wilson lattice gauge theory yields a theory satisfying the Wightman axioms.
milestones.criterion: For a Wilson lattice family with compact simple gauge group, remove the lattice cutoff at fixed physical volume. Obtain limiting correlations on ℝ⁴ along a common subsequence of increasing volumes. In a pure phase of the limit, establish the Osterwalder–Schrader conditions and reconstruct relativistic fields satisfying the Wightman axioms.
milestones.set_by: Yang–Mills group, October submission assessment, §§5–6, applying Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction.
milestones.threshold_quote: a relativistic quantum field theory satisfying the Wightman axioms can be constructed as a scaling limit

not_found: No statement by a mathematical society or prize body disputing the value or achievability of the combined goal was found.

results.finding: Finite-volume Wilson moments use normalized plaquette weights and product Haar measure in one lattice family per eligible gauge group.
results.quote: Finite moments integrate products of local insertions against the normalized exponential of the plaquette action on the given group, with product Haar measure.

results.finding: One Wilson family per eligible gauge group yields a subsequential continuum hierarchy with a selected Wightman reconstruction.
results.detail: The contact extension agrees with separated correlations. The source explicitly excludes raw cutoff convergence on collision diagonals from its claim.
results.quote: For each closed matrix subgroup with nonabelian simple real Lie algebra, choose one Wilson lattice family. For every strictly increasing sequence of volumes, it has a subsequence and a continuum hierarchy with the following properties.

results.finding: Wilson constructs exactly gauge-invariant pure gauge observables on a finite 4-dimensional lattice at positive spacing.
results.detail: This is a mathematical construction with no empirical sample size. The non-Abelian extension is stated briefly, with measure invariance implicit in the group integration prescription.
results.quote:
It is shown how to quantize a gauge field theory
on a discrete lattice in Euclidean space-time, preserving exact gauge invariance and treating the gauge
fields as angular variables {which makes a gauge-fixing term unnecessary).

results.finding: In 4 dimensions, one common volume subsequence per compact simple gauge group gives a Wilson lattice limit with a pure-phase Wightman reconstruction.
results.detail: The result is a theorem, so sample size is inapplicable. Lattice convergence is proved away from coincident points. The independent Osterwalder–Schrader comparison checks the centered stress-tensor trace in the selected phase, and the checked construction links that phase to the reconstructed fields.
results.quote:
Any chosen subsequential limit admits a decomposition into component theories (pure phases), each
proven to satisfy the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms. Then, through the OS reconstruction theorem
(also proven in the submission) this defines a QFT satisfying the Wightman axioms.

In each such theory there must be an energy \u0394 > 0 such that every excitation lies at least \u0394 above the vacuum, the state of lowest energy.". Reason: The definition should specify infinite space-time and make clear that the same positive bound applies to every excitation of a given theory.
